claim_verdicts.evidence: Core concepts: "Sync status: Whether or not the live state matches the target state." "Target state: The desired state of an application, as represented by files in a Git repository." Execution (gitops-first-sync.txt:3-24): every object OutOfSync while none exists; Synced after the sync (40-60). staging-manual.yaml:16 `targetRevision: main` matches "for `staging`, the branch `main`".

Sync Options (Server-Side Apply / Replace): "By default, Argo CD executes the `kubectl apply` operation to apply the configuration stored in Git." Core concepts: "Sync: The process of making an application move to its target state. E.g. by applying changes to a Kubernetes cluster."

Automated Sync Policy: "Argo CD has the ability to automatically sync an application when it detects differences"; the `automated` policy is set under `spec.syncPolicy`, and with `spec.syncPolicy.automated.enabled` false "the controller skips automated sync". FAQ: after Git changes are detected, only applications with auto-sync enabled are updated. It is the automated part of syncPolicy, not syncPolicy as such, that starts syncs. staging-manual.yaml has no syncPolicy; execution: nothing applied until the patch (txt:3, 26-28).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: An automated sync policy (spec.syncPolicy.automated) is what lets Argo CD start syncs by itself; an Application without one, such as staging-manual.yaml with no syncPolicy at all, reports OutOfSync and waits until someone starts a sync.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Health page: priority "`Healthy`, `Suspended`, `Progressing`, `Missing`, `Degraded`, `Unknown`"; "`Progressing` - the resource is not healthy yet but still making progress"; Deployment checks: "Observed generation is equal to desired generation." "Number of updated replicas equals the number of desired replicas." Docs omit availability; execution settles it: Progressing at READY 0/2, UP-TO-DATE 2 (= desired), AVAILABLE 0; Healthy at AVAILABLE 2 (txt:29-38).

Health page: "The App health will be the worst health of its immediate child sources." Priority: Healthy, Suspended, Progressing, Missing, Degraded, Unknown. The rule is worst-health-wins among objects that have a health; ConfigMaps in envs/staging have no health check, yet staging ends Healthy (txt:34-36). The lesson's "if any object is not `Healthy`, neither is the Application" reads as if every object must itself be Healthy.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: An Application's health is the worst health among the objects it manages, so if any object reports a health worse than Healthy, such as Progressing, the Application reports it too.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Health page lists `Missing` in the priority order (no further definition). Execution: before the first sync, with no object of envs/staging in donhang, app_wait prints "staging: OutOfSync, Missing" (txt:3); since the Application takes the worst object health and nothing else is present, the objects' health is Missing.

Resource tracking: annotation mode is "(default)"; Argo CD "uses the `argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id` annotation to track application resources"; label mode works "by setting the application instance label to the name of the managing Application on all resources". Annotations page: tracking-id "Used by Argo CD to track resources it manages." No page says the mark is written during a sync on each applied object. Namespace part verified: no Namespace in status.resources, script prints "no" (txt:62-63).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Argo CD looks only at manifests in the Application's path and live objects carrying its tracking annotation (argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id), which every object it manages has; namespace donhang (made by OpenTofu, no manifest in envs/staging) is neither: not in status.resources, not reported missing, not changed.

claim_verdicts.evidence: FAQ: "The default maximum polling interval is 3 minutes (120 seconds + 60 seconds jitter)." Annotations: argocd.argoproj.io/refresh, values `normal`, `hard`: "Indicates that app needs to be refreshed." "Removed by application controller after app is refreshed." Core concepts: "Refresh: Compare the latest code in Git with the live state." gitops.sh:106 sets refresh=normal. Lesson states no interval value.

Sync with kubectl: a sync is triggered "by applying or patching the Argo CD application with a document that defines an operation" (`kubectl patch -n <namespace> app <app-name> --patch-file <patch-file> --type merge`); "the state of the synchronization is reported in the operationState field", example `phase: Succeeded`. `sync.revision` is not shown there; execution settles it: script :31-32 patch, :33-37 poll, output "sync: Succeeded" (txt:26-28).
